title: Criminal Code Amendment (Private Sexual Material) Bill 2016
short_title: Criminal Code Amendment (Private Sexual Material) Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create offences addressing non-consensual sharing of private sexual material through telecommunications, related threats and preparation of material for use in those offences.
Sharing and threat offences would carry maximum prison terms of three years, while preparation for commercial purposes or another benefit would attract up to five years.
Covered material would include sexual images or depictions that a reasonable person in the subject’s circumstances would expect to remain private, with specified statutory defences.
changes: A threat could be prosecuted even if the material does not exist or the recipient does not actually fear it.
Sending private sexual material to its subject would be excluded from the sharing offence.
A defence would cover specified media activities where its conditions, including a reasonable public interest belief, are satisfied.
Prosecuting a person under 18 would require the Attorney-General’s consent.
summary.affected: People depicted in private sexual material, recipients of threats and people sharing, threatening or preparing such material are affected.
